cards.title: Map and Answer Top Pre-Purchase Objections on Product Pages
cards.summary: Identify the 10 objections blocking a purchase for each key product and answer them in dedicated content linked from the PDP.
cards.use_when: Building or auditing a product page (PDP) for a category where buyers hesitate because they cannot touch, test or ask a salesperson about the product.

cards.title: Use Personalized Discovery to Lift Homepage-to-PDP Conversion
cards.summary: Serve product recommendations based on each visitor's browsing affinity and add frequently-bought-together modules to build confidence and revenue.
cards.use_when: Merchandising the homepage, category pages or PDPs when you want to increase product-page views and average basket size without new traffic.

cards.title: Build a Three-Step Automated Post-Purchase Communication Flow
cards.summary: Send order confirmation, shipping confirmation and out-for-delivery notifications automatically to eliminate most Where-Is-My-Order anxiety.
cards.use_when: Designing or auditing the transactional email/SMS flow between checkout and delivery for an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Exploit the 'Quiet Period' Between Order and Delivery
cards.summary: Treat the window after purchase but before delivery as a relationship-building period using education, onboarding and community content.
cards.use_when: Planning lifecycle messaging for stores where delivery takes days and customers are switching from a familiar product or brand.

cards.title: Replace Carrier Tracking Links with a Branded Tracking Page
cards.summary: Reclaim the frequently visited tracking moment as an owned revenue and retention surface instead of redirecting customers to a generic carrier site.
cards.use_when: Setting up shipping confirmation emails and tracking for a Shopify or similar store whose customers currently land on a carrier's generic tracking page.

cards.title: Turn Tracking Pages into Multi-Visit Selling Channels
cards.summary: Customers check tracking ~4.6 times per order; each visit is a chance to cross-sell, educate and drive loyalty.
cards.use_when: Deciding what modules to place on the branded tracking page and how to measure its revenue contribution.

cards.title: Design an Unboxing Protocol with Insert Cards, Notes and Unexpected Gifts
cards.summary: Layer a standard insert card plus selective handwritten notes and small surprises onto the one physical touchpoint you control.
cards.use_when: Designing packaging, packing slips and inserts for fulfillment, and deciding which order types justify higher-touch treatment.

cards.title: Use Packaging and Inserts as a Full-Funnel Creative Asset
cards.summary: Treat unboxing as a content system whose output feeds earned media and acquisition, not just a fulfillment cost.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in custom packaging and how to justify it against acquisition spend.

cards.title: Time reassurance, product education and replenishment to the actual order journey
cards.summary: Combat buyer's remorse with a timed reassurance email, then follow with education and replenishment prompts.
cards.use_when: Building the post-purchase email sequence in Klaviyo or a similar platform for any considered-purchase product.

cards.title: Trigger product education around confirmed delivery and first use
cards.summary: Send quick-start, tutorial and common-mistakes emails within three days of delivery for any product requiring setup or learning.
cards.use_when: Planning post-delivery emails for products that require assembly, configuration or technique, where misuse drives returns.

cards.title: Test faster refunds with clear customer choice and eligibility
cards.summary: Collapse the refund timeline from 10–14 days to seconds or minutes to recapture purchase intent at its peak.
cards.use_when: Selecting a refund method or negotiating refund timelines with your returns platform and finance team.

cards.title: Run a Recovery Playbook That Over-Fixes Complaints
cards.summary: Empower support to exceed the standard fix, because customers whose problems were solved well can become the strongest advocates.
cards.use_when: Writing customer service policy and defining how much latitude agents have when a delivery or product fails.

cards.title: Shift Loyalty from Points-Only to Experiential Rewards
cards.summary: Replace or supplement discount-based points with VIP access, events, line passes and recognition to differentiate your program.
cards.use_when: Designing or revamping a loyalty program and choosing reward mechanics for a young or fashion-driven customer base.

cards.title: Integrate Rewards Into Checkout and Measure Redemption Uplift
cards.summary: In-checkout redemption and one-to-one experiences track to higher LTV among members who actually redeem.
cards.use_when: Deciding how members redeem rewards and which metrics prove the loyalty program is working.

cards.title: Segment Post-Purchase Flows by First-Time, Repeat and VIP Buyers
cards.summary: Build distinct post-purchase email flows per customer segment, using education for new buyers and early access for VIPs.
cards.use_when: Restructuring lifecycle email and on-site experience so loyal customers do not receive the same treatment as first-time shoppers.

cards.title: Run Post-Checkout Upsells to Increase Basket Value
cards.summary: Offer a complementary or larger-size product immediately after checkout, on the thank-you page or in a follow-up email.
cards.use_when: Adding an upsell/cross-sell mechanic to the checkout completion or thank-you page without disrupting the purchase.

cards.title: Track Delight Metrics Alongside Retention Metrics
cards.summary: Measure emotional-connection metrics such as UGC generation and return-to-repurchase rate, not just CSAT and NPS.
cards.use_when: Setting up the reporting dashboard that proves whether post-purchase investments are paying off.

cards.title: Sequencing Rule: Fix Effortlessness Before Adding Delight
cards.summary: Delight only compounds loyalty when delivery, returns and product quality are already frictionless.
cards.use_when: Prioritizing a post-purchase roadmap or deciding whether to invest in notes and gifts versus fixing shipping and refund operations.

cards.title: Define Lifetime Gross Profit with a Time Constraint
cards.summary: Calculate LTGP as revenue minus COGS, delivery, fees and refunds, always anchored to a fixed window like 30/90/180 days.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much you can afford to pay for new customers, or setting the retention and LTV targets your store will be managed against.

cards.title: Prioritize the Retention Hierarchy Before Touching Email and SMS
cards.summary: Fix product quality, product portfolio, acquisition quality and customer experience before expecting owned media to rescue retention.
cards.use_when: Repeat purchase rate or 90-day LTV is flat and you're tempted to invest in more email flows, SMS or Klaviyo work as the first fix.

cards.title: Set a CAC Target from LTGP and an Efficiency Ratio
cards.summary: Divide the chosen LTGP window by a target LTGP:CAC ratio (2-3 for scaling) to get your CAC ceiling.
cards.use_when: Setting paid media bid and budget ceilings, or judging whether current CAC is efficient for your store's growth appetite.

cards.title: Estimate a scenario bound for paid acquisition cost from CPC and conversion
cards.summary: Use CPC divided by click-to-new-customer conversion for a consistent paid-traffic scenario, not an immutable CAC floor.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in more paid media efficiency or in retention and LTV instead, or sanity-checking an over-optimistic CAC forecast.

cards.title: Use CAC Payback Period for Subscription-first Brands
cards.summary: When first-purchase gross profit is below CAC, track the point at which cumulative subscription or replenishment profit repays the deficit.
cards.use_when: Running a supplements, CPG or subscription store that knowingly loses money on the first order.

cards.title: Decide the LTGP Window by Growth Appetite and Capital
cards.summary: Extend the payback window (30 to 90 to 180 days) only when you have the capital to fund losses on new customers and the modelling skill to manage it.
cards.use_when: Choosing whether to fund aggressive paid acquisition now by allowing a longer payback, or to stay conservative and cash-positive on first purchase.

cards.title: Separate period returning-customer rate from cohort repeat purchase
cards.summary: A period customer-mix measure can rise when new-customer acquisition falls; use mature cohorts to assess repeat purchase.
cards.use_when: Reviewing your store's repeat purchase health in Shopify analytics or recommending retention improvements based on that dashboard.

cards.title: Inspect Which Half of the LTGP:CAC Ratio to Work On
cards.summary: CAC has a hard floor and LTGP a practical ceiling; estimate both first, then invest in the side with real headroom.
cards.use_when: Choosing between funding more paid media optimisation or funding retention, offer, bundle and subscription programs.

cards.title: Balance Attribution and Profitability Metrics in Your Owned Media KPIs
cards.summary: Use Klaviyo attribution as a north-star indicator but drive day-to-day decisions from profitability metrics — and avoid the two extremes.
cards.use_when: Setting the reporting dashboard for your email/SMS retention program, or deciding what changes your retention team should make.

cards.title: Focus on Pop-up Conversion Rather Than Opt-in Rate
cards.summary: Judge pop-ups by the AOV, gross profit and conversion rate of signed-up customers, not by the opt-in percentage.
cards.use_when: Designing or reviewing a signup pop-up and deciding whether the captured audience is worth making new-customer content for.

cards.title: Map the Customer Journey as F1/F2/F3 Functions and Structure Flows Around It
cards.summary: Organize every flow into acquisition, first-to-second order conversion, and top-20% loyalty stages so you can isolate and fix any constraint.
cards.use_when: Restructuring your Klaviyo account or asking 'where do I go to fix' when repeat purchase or LTV underperforms.

cards.title: Segment Campaigns for Reach, Not Hyperpersonalization
cards.summary: Send elite content to as many engaged people as possible most of the time; reserve narrow segments for specific goals.
cards.use_when: Planning campaign sends and choosing whether to slice your email/SMS list into niche audiences.

cards.title: Find eligible subscribers missed by overly narrow campaign segments
cards.summary: A 9-figure retailer was only reaching around 200k of 750k profiles; fixing the engaged-audience structure meant campaign peaks could reach far more people.
cards.use_when: Planning a sale, launch or restock and wondering how much of the email list will actually receive the message.

cards.title: Plan Lifecycle Cohorts by Purchase and Subscription Stage
cards.summary: Map customers into never-purchased, purchased-but-not-subscribed, active subscriber and cancelled subscriber cohorts to set clear per-cohort goals.
cards.use_when: Designing retention strategy for a subscription or replenishment store and deciding what each part of the customer base should receive.

cards.title: Prioritize retention tests by the constraint in the customer journey
cards.summary: A/B testing should target the identified constraint with structural, offer or messaging changes rather than cosmetic email optimisation.
cards.use_when: Directing a retention team's testing roadmap, or asking what to test after the email flows have been built.

cards.title: Map Campaign Revenue to Calendar Peaks and Engagement Build
cards.summary: Repeat customer revenue arrives as waves tied to sales, launches and restocks, so year-round audience engagement is what creates the peaks.
cards.use_when: Planning your campaign calendar and deciding how much to invest in engagement-building content outside of sale periods.

cards.title: Measure Retention at 30/60/90/180/365 Day Cohorts and Top-20% Revenue
cards.summary: Track LTGP-adjusted cohort curves by time window and revenue from the top 20% of customers to find where retention is lagging.
cards.use_when: Building a retention dashboard or answering 'is our retention programme actually working' with real numbers.

cards.title: Diagnose weak second-purchase conversion before blaming email copy
cards.summary: Sustained second-purchase failure usually traces to unaddressed retention foundations and the absence of a mapped customer journey.
cards.use_when: Interpreting a poor repeat purchase rate and deciding whether the issue is execution (emails) or foundations (product, portfolio, acquisition, experience).

cards.title: Plan a Bundled, Subscription-first Offer Structure to Raise LTGP
cards.summary: Restructure bundles, front-end offers and subscription options to lift the LTGP ceiling within a 90-365 day window.
cards.use_when: Working the LTGP side of the LTGP:CAC ratio instead of pushing further on paid efficiency.

cards.title: Build and grow an engaged subscriber segment
cards.summary: Define an engaged audience using email and on-site behaviors, then expand reach by slowly re-introducing dormant subscribers in random chunks.
cards.use_when: You are planning a retention or email marketing operation and need to decide who to send to, or you want to grow reachable subscribers ahead of a major sale.

cards.title: Use flows for personalization, campaigns for reach
cards.summary: Reserve behavior-triggered flows for one-to-one personalization and use broader campaigns for reach and brand moments.
cards.use_when: You are deciding how to allocate effort between automated flows and broadcast campaigns, or where to apply personalization in your email/SMS program.

cards.title: Define VIPs by revenue and profit share
cards.summary: Identify VIPs as the segment driving roughly 50%+ of revenue and ~80% of profit, then decide whether to invest in them based on your actual constraint.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to build VIP campaigns, a loyalty program, or VIP flow pathways, or deciding whether first-to-second order conversion should take priority.

cards.title: Run RFM analysis to segment on real purchase behavior
cards.summary: Score subscribers on Recency, Frequency, and Monetary value relative to your own customer base to build actionable cohorts.
cards.use_when: You are building customer segments for win-back flows, replenishment, VIP campaigns, or first-to-second order conversion.

cards.title: Use paid ads to surface new arrivals to existing customers
cards.summary: For fashion and drop-driven brands, allocate dedicated paid spend to existing customers to surface new products, measured against tighter efficiency KPIs.
cards.use_when: You run frequent product drops or new arrivals and need to decide whether to spend paid media against your existing customer base.

cards.title: Audit discount-acquired cohorts for LTV quality
cards.summary: Acquire customers on discount only after checking whether those cohorts have worse repeat rates, which the source says affects a majority of brands.
cards.use_when: You are planning promotions or discount-driven acquisition (e.g., BFCM) and deciding whether the front-end performance reflects true customer value.

cards.title: Use zero-party data to improve acquisition targeting
cards.summary: Collect zero-party data (customer preferences, problems, motivations) to define personas and angles, then feed top- and bottom-customer insights back into paid ads.
cards.use_when: You are designing acquisition creative, personas, or angles, or setting up post-purchase surveys to inform paid media.

cards.title: Measure engaged-segment growth as your core retention KPI
cards.summary: Track the size of your engaged audience over time as the primary email retention metric, rather than optimizing each broadcast in isolation.
cards.use_when: You are setting retention KPIs, reviewing email/SMS performance, or deciding whether a reactivation strategy is working.

cards.title: Reward VIPs with exclusivity rather than broad discounts
cards.summary: Give VIPs exclusive products, early access, perks, and experiences instead of treating them like the general list.
cards.use_when: You are designing VIP campaigns, a loyalty program, or flow pathways and want to increase VIP revenue without cheapening the relationship.

cards.title: Define desired customer emotions before designing the experience
cards.summary: Work backwards from the feelings and behaviors you want customers to have rather than pitching a product first.
cards.use_when: Designing your store's overall experience strategy, or briefing any change to the PDP, cart, post-purchase email or packaging.

cards.title: Put a 'customer chair' in your merchandising decisions
cards.summary: Use an explicit customer-perspective check so customer needs appear on the agenda before business metrics do.
cards.use_when: Running a weekly trading, merchandising or roadmap meeting for your store where decisions about products, promotions or site changes get made.

cards.title: Assess where your store sits on the random-to-differentiated CX spectrum
cards.summary: Diagnose whether your customer experience is accidental, designed or differentiated, and budget years not quarters for the transition.
cards.use_when: Reviewing your post-purchase experience and deciding how much to invest in standardising it versus differentiating it.

cards.title: Rank what customers actually value before your product
cards.summary: Corporate attitude, ease of business and helpful support outrank product quality in customers' ranking of favourite brands.
cards.use_when: Prioritising the retention and post-purchase roadmap: which improvement to fund first in support, ease, personalisation or product.

cards.title: Use purpose and word of mouth instead of pure differentiation on product
cards.summary: Products, price and quality are hard to differentiate, so treat experience and advocacy as the competitive edge.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to invest for competitive advantage in a crowded product category or a store selling easily-copied goods.

cards.title: Ask employees what customers think before surveying customers
cards.summary: Skip intrusive surveys and start with front-line employee judgement plus data you already hold.
cards.use_when: Setting up or rethinking your store's voice-of-customer measurement, satisfaction tracking or post-purchase feedback programme.

cards.title: Map the customer journey, not your internal processes
cards.summary: Journey mapping is the core tool for seeing the experience as the customer lives it and deciding where to focus improvements.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing where your post-purchase experience breaks down and deciding which fulfilment, email or support step to fix first.

cards.title: Run the three-part CX framework: strategy, measurement, people
cards.summary: Apply a simple framework covering intended experience, journey-based measurement and the culture that enables delivery.
cards.use_when: Structuring a customer experience programme across your store's merchandising, fulfilment, support and team.

cards.title: Define who your customer is, emotionally as well as demographically
cards.summary: Before deciding the experience, know customers' motivators, attitudes, values and purposes beyond your product.
cards.use_when: Building customer personas or researching buyers to inform PDP copy, post-purchase messaging and retention offers.

cards.title: Write a customer experience strategy as an umbrella over the whole store
cards.summary: Define what you want customers to feel across the journey and translate it into principles and practical actions.
cards.use_when: Creating a documented CX strategy that governs store design, fulfilment choices, support tone and team behaviour.

cards.title: Give the CX function cross-functional ownership, led from the top
cards.summary: Customer experience is a leadership and culture question, not a marketing department job.
cards.use_when: Deciding who owns customer experience in a growing store team and how it connects across marketing, fulfilment and support.

cards.title: Create a shared experience vision to motivate front-line staff
cards.summary: Define what customers and employees should experience together so support staff can translate product pride into helping customers.
cards.use_when: Improving support quality, agent motivation and consistency in how your store's team handles customer problems.

cards.title: Apply the same CX principles to B2B and less emotional categories
cards.summary: B2B buyers are still people, so journey, strategy and measurement principles carry over unchanged.
cards.use_when: Selling to businesses, public sector or any buyer where you assume customer experience is a consumer-only concern.

cards.title: Make experience a deliberate design, not a chance outcome
cards.summary: Experiences happen whether or not you design them, so choose the experience and process deliberately.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much to standardise post-purchase touchpoints such as order confirmation, shipping updates, packaging and returns handling.

cards.title: Build a Bill of Materials Before Anything Else
cards.summary: A bill of materials breaks unit cost into every component and sub-vendor so COGS becomes a controllable, negotiable line instead of a mystery number.
cards.use_when: Setting up or renegotiating product sourcing for any physical-goods store, and before you start sourcing a new SKU or assume your landed cost is fixed.

cards.title: Use BOM to Rethink Product Specs, Not Just Costs
cards.summary: Once you see every component's cost, you can engineer margin by changing materials, karat purity, or SKU tiers rather than only squeezing the supplier.
cards.use_when: Merchandising and product-development decisions — deciding what materials, specs, and SKU variants to sell and at what price.

cards.title: Enter Supplier Negotiations From a Position of Redundancy
cards.summary: Before asking a supplier to cut cost, do your homework so you already know the benchmark cost and have alternate suppliers mapped — leverage comes from preparation.
cards.use_when: Preparing for a cost-down negotiation with a factory or new supplier, or onboarding a supplier for a new product line.

cards.title: Frame Cost-Downs as a Growth Partnership, Not a Squeeze
cards.summary: Present cost reduction to suppliers as fueling volume growth for both sides — share your P&L vision and translate it into units and dollars they care about.
cards.use_when: Making the first cost-down request to an existing factory, or resetting terms after acquiring a store or scaling a product line.

cards.title: Ask for Volume Price Breaks on Every BOM Line
cards.summary: Negotiate component-level price breaks tied to unit volumes, understanding that factory economics rest on machine and labor utilization.
cards.use_when: Setting up volume tiers with a factory, planning a purchase order schedule, or forecasting COGS at higher volumes.

cards.title: Use Payment Terms to Widen Your Float, Not to Chase Sales
cards.summary: Your real float is payment terms minus production lead time, so extending net terms buys you error tolerance and free cash flow.
cards.use_when: Deciding what payment terms to request from suppliers and how much working capital to hold before scaling ad spend or order volume.

cards.title: Understand Supplier Financing to Unlock Better Terms
cards.summary: Factories use credit insurance and invoice factoring, so your P&L, not just the PO, determines the terms you can get — clean books matter.
cards.use_when: Negotiating extended terms or consignment, and when a supplier says they can't afford to float you.

cards.title: Compare supplier credit with other working-capital options
cards.summary: The goal across BOM, price breaks and terms is a supplier relationship where they finance your inventory and dividends.
cards.use_when: Designing your overall sourcing/finance strategy and deciding what to prioritize as you scale purchasing.

cards.title: Build Component-Redundancy and Market-Monitoring Discipline
cards.summary: Actively re-source commodity components on an ongoing basis rather than one-time — keep multiple vendors and spot-check market prices.
cards.use_when: Managing replenishment and ongoing COGS after initial sourcing is set up.

cards.title: Pause Growth When Input and Tariff Shocks Hit
cards.summary: When duties, tariffs or commodity moves make the unit economics unsafe, it is acceptable to deliberately slow growth and hold flat while you rework sourcing.
cards.use_when: Fulfillment and sourcing planning when tariffs, duties, or input costs spike and your margins are compressed.

cards.title: Close Books Monthly and Dividend From Free Cash, Not EBITDA
cards.summary: Track actual cash generation monthly and fund only needed working capital before taking distributions — EBITDA is not cash.
cards.use_when: Setting a monthly schedule for taking money out of the store and deciding how much cash to retain to fund growth.

cards.title: Audit Margin Reality: COGS Is Your Biggest Lever
cards.summary: Opex and marketing are relatively predictable; COGS is the biggest controllable swing factor, which is why sourcing discipline beats growth-at-all-costs.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to spend optimization effort — sourcing vs marketing vs overhead — and reviewing whether your business is genuinely profitable in cash terms.

cards.title: Bill of Materials as the Foundation of Supply Chain Profit
cards.summary: A bill of material (BOM) is the foundational layer for any physical-goods business and the starting point for supply chain optimization and cash extraction.
cards.use_when: Setting up or auditing sourcing and COGS for a physical product store, or planning a cost-reduction or margin-improvement initiative across SKUs.

cards.title: Free Cash Flow vs. Enterprise Value: Which Game Is Your Store Playing
cards.summary: Businesses should be mapped on a quadrant of free cash flow versus enterprise value, because cash extraction tactics and exit options differ entirely between the two.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to optimize a store for ongoing cash distributions versus building a sellable, valued enterprise.

cards.title: Offer Optimization as the #1 Meta Scaling Lever
cards.summary: For most stuck Meta accounts, the biggest lever is a stale or weak offer rather than new creatives or bidding changes.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing a paid-social account that has plateaued despite healthy spend, or planning a growth push on a store in the $5–50M range.

cards.title: Rotating Hooks and Angles Before Adding Media Budget
cards.summary: When the offer is solid but the account is stuck, the bottleneck is breadth of hooks and angles for the product.
cards.use_when: Scaling creative testing on Meta or planning a new creative sprint for a single hero SKU.

cards.title: Influencer-Specific Landing Pages That Mirror the Ad
cards.summary: Matching the ad to a personalized collection page in the same order the products appeared produced a large conversion lift.
cards.use_when: Building or rebuilding landing pages for influencer or whitelisted ads, or diagnosing a creative-to-page mismatch killing conversion.

cards.title: Using Partnership Ads to Bridge the Trust Gap
cards.summary: Whitelisting creator content as partnership ads adds trust signals and diversity to a Meta account that standard brand ads cannot.
cards.use_when: Scaling paid social for high-AOV or considered-purchase products, or diversifying a Meta ad account dominated by brand-owned creatives.

cards.title: Paying Creators a Trial Daily Rate Before Committing
cards.summary: Compensate whitelisted creators with a fixed daily rate and a short trial window so media spend is predictable and risk is bounded.
cards.use_when: Negotiating influencer or partnership-ad deals when you cannot forecast whether the asset will convert.

cards.title: One-Day-Click ROAS with Post-Purchase Survey Multiplier
cards.summary: Use platform-independent 1-day click ROAS tempered by post-purchase survey data to extrapolate lifetime performance and judge whether an ad account can be scaled profitably.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to scale spend on Meta and other channels when multi-touch attribution is judged unreliable, especially for considered-purchase products.
